title.en: How Does Your Small Creative Idea Catch Fire?
title.zh: 一个小创意来了，你会先怎么接？

description.en: Six recreational idea choices follow a surprising prompt, a rough working version or a willing listener. Find your idea-start portrait.
description.zh: 六次休闲创意选择，跟意外提示、粗糙试版或愿意听的人，看想法怎样开始。

introduction.en: Choose for one low-stakes creative idea, not your work performance. The result describes an approach in this game; it does not identify a fixed creative type, learning style or level of talent.
introduction.zh: 只为一个轻松创意选，不评工作表现。结果描述本游戏中的做法，不认定固定创意类型、学习风格或才华高低。

focus.en: Starting a small idea by changing the prompt, making a rough version or testing how another willing person understands it.
focus.zh: 换提示、造粗版或听愿意者怎样理解，启动小想法。

prompt.en: You want a small new idea. You begin by…

label.en: Combining two ordinary things that do not usually meet.
label.zh: 把两件不常相遇的普通物相配。

label.en: Making the simplest visible version of a vague thought.
label.zh: 把模糊念头做成最简单可见版。

label.en: Telling a willing friend one sentence and hearing their question.
label.zh: 向愿意朋友说一句，听其问题。

prompt.en: The first attempt feels flat. You…

label.en: Change one part of the rough version and compare.
Ask what another person actually understood.
label.zh: 问别人实际理解到什么。

label.en: Change one constraint to generate a different possibility.

prompt.en: You have ten casual minutes. You choose…

label.en: One brief conversation about the idea, with permission.
Several unusual starting prompts without finishing them.
label.zh: 列几条奇起点，不用做完。

label.en: One rough sketch or mock version to react to.
label.zh: 一粗画或样版，让自己回应。

label.en: Use it to pose a different little question.
Put it into the rough version and see what changes.
Explain the detail and notice which part interests a listener.
label.zh: 解释细节，看听者对哪处有兴趣。

prompt.en: You decide whether to continue. You most want…
prompt.zh: 决定要不要继续，你最想……

label.en: A concrete version that makes the next change visible.
A question that still feels enjoyable to explore.
A clearer sense of what the idea communicates.
label.zh: 更清楚想法传达了什么。

prompt.en: Your small idea can stop when…

label.en: The conversation has answered the question I brought.
label.zh: 对话已答我带来的问题。

label.en: The trial has shown me enough for today.
label.zh: 试版已给今天足够信息。

label.en: The playful possibility was enjoyable even without an output.
label.zh: 可能本身有趣，无产出也可。

summary.en: Your idea starts by changing the invitation. An unusual combination or a different constraint gives an ordinary subject another possible direction without requiring a completely original discovery.
summary.zh: 你的创意从改邀请开始。意外组合或不同限制给普通主题另一路，不要求全新发现。

example.en: You might ask what a postcard would look like if it could describe only sounds, then enjoy a few possible answers.
example.zh: 你可问明信片若只能写声音会怎样，享受几个可能答案。

strength.en: A fresh prompt can loosen a familiar starting point and generate alternatives before you commit effort to making any one version.
strength.zh: 新问法可松开熟悉起点，在投入造某版前生成替代。

tradeoff.en: New prompts can keep replacing each other without giving one idea time to develop. Choosing a single small trial remains available whenever you want it.
tradeoff.zh: 新提示会一直相替，不给一想法发展。愿意时仍可选一个小试。

experiment.en: Take an ordinary fictional object and change one harmless constraint. Write three possible responses, then choose whether any deserves a tiny sketch.
experiment.zh: 选普通虚构物，换一无害限制，写三回应，再选是否值得画小图。

summary.en: Your idea becomes interesting when something is available to respond to. A rough version is a question made visible, not an early examination of whether your final work will be good.
summary.zh: 有东西可回应时，你的点子活起来。粗版是可见提问，不是提前考试成品好坏。

example.en: A folded scrap with a penciled handle might help you understand an imagined object more quickly than another page of plans.
example.zh: 折纸片添铅笔把手，可能比再写一页计划更快理解想象物。

strength.en: A small working image can reveal specific decisions and make the next revision more concrete than a general wish to improve the idea.
strength.zh: 小试图显出具体决定，让修改比笼统“更好”具体。

tradeoff.en: A rough version can become expensive if you keep polishing it before learning anything. The trial only needs enough detail to answer one question.
tradeoff.zh: 没学到东西就不断打磨，粗版也贵。只需足够细节答一个问题。

experiment.en: Make a thirty-second sketch of a harmless idea and write the one question it helps answer. Stop before improving details unrelated to that question.
experiment.zh: 三十秒画无害点子，写它帮答的一问题。无关细节先别磨。

summary.en: Your idea takes shape through a voluntary exchange. Another person’s question shows what your words actually communicate without making their approval the measure of whether the idea deserves to exist.
summary.zh: 你的想法经自愿交流成形。别人问题显出话传了什么，不把赞同当存在资格。

example.en: A friend might ask which part of your imaginary exhibition a visitor would try first, helping you notice an assumption you had not explained.
example.zh: 朋友问想象展中访客先试哪处，帮你发现未解释的假定。

strength.en: A willing listener can provide a different view of an idea and help separate what is clear to its maker from what was actually shared.
strength.zh: 愿意听者给另视角，区分作者自己清楚与实际说出的部分。

tradeoff.en: Feedback can pull an idea in several directions. You can thank a listener and still choose which question, if any, you want to act on.
tradeoff.zh: 反馈会拉多向。可谢听者，仍自己选要不要、回应哪问。

experiment.en: If someone wants to listen, describe a tiny fictional idea in one sentence and ask what they pictured. Treat their answer as information, not a verdict.
experiment.zh: 有人愿听时，一句讲虚构点子，问想到什么画面。把回答当信息，不当判决。
